title: Pinecrest FinServ - initial discovery scratchpad
content:
Context: 11/05 call with Pinecrest Financial Services (Pinecrest).

Attendees: Pinecrest: Aisha Khan (PM), Daniel Morris (Infra lead), Priya Rao (Legal/compliance)
Redwood: Maya (SE), Liam (solutions), Sofia (product SME)

High-level ask: Evaluate embedding/search + chat assistant to help frontline agents answer compliance and product questions. Must satisfy financial data handling rules, SOC2-like audit, and contractually required data residency (EU) for some lines of business.

Notes / raw capture:
- They said: "Need something we can trust with transaction metadata (non-PII) but _never_ send raw account numbers or SSNs to third-party clouds."
- Primary use cases: agent assist (chat summarization, suggested replies), internal knowledge base search (embeddings), and automated triage for escalations.
- Volume estimate (they're fuzzy): ~250 agents, peak 30 qps for embeddings/candidates; typical chat gen QPS 10-15 during peak.
- Latency target for agent-assist: <150ms p50 for token generation (goal), p95 <300ms. Agents will abandon if slower.
- SLA expectation: 99.9% availability for prod; for POC they are ok with lower but want a roadmap to production SLAs.

Regulatory / security constraints (from Priya):
- Data residency: EU-only for EU customer interactions (must support region routing).
- KMS/HSM: keys must be customer-managed for any customer PII that is persisted.
- Audit logs: retention 7 years for certain transcripts (yikes). Need proof we can export immutable logs to their SIEM.
- Redaction: prefer client-side redaction before tokens sent to us. They want optional Redwood-managed redaction + deterministic redaction hooks.
- Legal wants a technical spec for our data deletion/retention flow, plus a list of subprocessors.

Deployment posture discussed:
- They pushed hard for Private (VPC) deployment — reason: control + auditability.
- They asked about on-prem appliance for air-gapped pockets; said they have a pilot group that may be air-gapped.
- Dedicated vs hosted: they asked about cost delta — we need to prepare a two-tier TCO (Dedicated reserved vs Private on their cloud) with rough monthly numbers.

Model / capability requirements:
- Need embeddings comparable to OpenAI/text-embedding-3-small or better for semantic search across KBs.
- Chat model must support system messages + function/tool calling (for dynamic content fetch).
- Deterministic output not required but they will want guardrails for hallucinations (reliance on tool outputs + retrieval + citation).

Integration notes / flow they described: 
1) Agent UI calls our inference endpoint for suggested replies when agent clicks "assist".
2) Input pipeline: agent UI -> redaction filter -> retrieval (their vector DB) -> Redwood model API -> enriched response (with citations) -> agent.
3) Some transcripts saved to S3 in EU region; events forwarded to Splunk.

Gotchas / risk flags (brain dump):
- If client insists on client-managed KMS for all keys, hosted offering might not be acceptable. Need to map which keys can be CMK and which are Redwood-managed.
- Log retention 7 years is long; confirm storage costs and whether logs must be encrypted with CMK.
- On-prem request adds ops complexity: we need clear boundary of support levels and which features are available (e.g., can we ship Optimize suggestions if private?).
- Legal will push for subprocessors list and DPA SLA / breach notification windows.
- Rate-shaping: their peak QPS and concurrency means we’ll need dedicated capacity or autoscale policy. Initial POC can run smaller footprint but must be demonstrably scalable.

POC scope proposal (notes to self) - narrow and practical:
- Goal: demonstrate agent-assist + vector retrieval with EU residency and audit trail.
- Duration: 6 weeks: week 0 prep/security review, week 1-2 ingest small KB + embedding sync, week 3 integrate agent UI + redaction, week 4-5 tuning, week 6 review + handoff.
- Minimal infra: Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 (or private VPC if they insist), small embedding job (50k docs) + 2 serving nodes for chat.
- Acceptance criteria: p50 latency <150ms on test agent flows (avg 5k tokens/day), correct citation > 90% on QA set, successful export of audit logs to their Splunk instance, and integration with their KMS for persisted artifacts.

Action items (owner, rough due):
- Maya: Draft POC scope + high-level cost estimate (Dedicated vs Private) — due 11/10.
- Liam: Technical appendix on private deployment (what components, support matrix, CMK integration notes) — due 11/12.
- Sofia: Prepare short slide: risk/mitigations (redaction approach, log retention, model choice) — due 11/09.
- Maya: Ask Legal for subprocessors list + sample DPA (internal) to share with Pinecrest — due 11/07.
- Pinecrest (Aisha): Provide example KB export + sample redaction rules (they promised by next sync).

Open questions to resolve before next call:
- Which exact elements must use customer-managed keys? (transcript storage? embeddings at rest? logs?)
- Are there any regulatory constraints beyond EU residency (e.g., Swiss/UK specifics)?
- Can they accept redaction heuristics that we provide or do they require deterministic pre-send scrub?
- What is their expected retention window for non-regulated transcripts (we can propose 90 days)?

Sample prompts / testing ideas to include in POC:
- Prompt for agent assist: "You are a compliant customer support assistant. Given the conversation below and the retrieved documents, suggest a short reply with a citation to the KB doc IDs. Avoid asking for or exposing PII. If you are unsure, respond with 'escalate'."
- Test case for hallucination: provide question about obscure regulatory rule and ensure model falls back to 'no confident answer' rather than fabricate.

Rough cost/back-of-envelope (for internal use):
- Dedicated reserved (eu-west-1, 2x A10G-class nodes for 6 weeks inclusive of storage + embeddings job): estimate $12k–$18k for POC (very rough).
- Private deployment (customer VPC with node sizing + setup): one-time setup 2–4 weeks + professional services 30–60k depending on on-prem needs.

Next call: schedule week of 11/17 per Aisha. Prep: bring: short spec for KMS mapping, demo plan (what we can show live), and POC SOW outline.

Notes-to-self style:
- Emphasize retrieval + citation — lowers hallucination risk and is a big selling point.
- Prep a short checklist for compliance (region mapping, CMK mapping, log endpoints, data flow diagram).
- Check with infra on current EU capacity and Dedicated slot availability for mid-Nov start.

Misc: copy of the audio and meeting transcript uploaded to internal drive (link in CONF-1452).

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya"
